question: The GeM portal is down while incubator controller worth Rs. 1,560,000 is urgently needed for a pilot plant shutdown window. The section wants to buy offline immediately. What documentation makes that choice defensible?
expected_answer:
The case needs evidence, not just a statement that the portal was unavailable.
Screenshots, timestamps, urgency justification, and a note on why waiting was impractical should appear on file before any alternative route is taken.
key_points: Capture GeM downtime evidence
Record urgency and why delay was unacceptable
Explain why the alternative route was necessary
Apply the normal value route once the GeM exception is justified

question: The laboratory director wants to buy biological safety cabinet worth Rs. 310,000 from a local vendor because the same item looks cheaper outside GeM. GeM shows a similar listing. Can the buyer leave GeM on price alone?
expected_answer:
No. Price alone is usually not enough to bypass GeM when the item is available there.
The file should first examine GeM applicability under Rule 149; only a real specification gap, non-availability, or properly recorded exception can justify moving to LPC.
key_points: Check GeM availability first
Treat lower offline price as insufficient by itself
Record any specification mismatch or non-availability evidence
After a valid GeM departure, use the normal value route under Rule 155

question: The base price for calibration gases was noted as Rs. 3,110,000, but mandatory freight, installation, and AMC bring the realistic total to Rs. 3,150,000. The draft note still wants to use the lower route chosen on base price. Which valuation should control?
expected_answer:
The controlling value should be the realistic procurement value, not the stripped base price.
If mandatory charges move the case upward, the route should be re-tested on Rs. 3,150,000 and may need to shift to LTE under Rule 162.
key_points: Aggregate mandatory cost components
Do not choose route on an artificially reduced base price
Revise the estimate if the total changes the slab
Re-open the route if the controlling band changes

expected_answer:
A single valid offer does not automatically make the award unsafe, but it does require recorded scrutiny of competition and reasonableness.
The committee should review publicity, specification restrictiveness, urgency, and value for money before deciding whether to re-tender or proceed with competent approval under Rule 155.
key_points: Test whether competition was adequate
Examine if specifications were too restrictive
Record price reasonableness and urgency if proceeding
Take competent authority approval on the single-offer decision

question: A purchase committee convener proposes to break a Rs. 640,000 requirement for tissue culture flasks into 2 indents of about Rs. 320,000 each for a student training programme starting next week so the case stays below a higher route. What compliance issue arises? The price looks attractive, so the team wants to overlook a control weakness. Would you clear the note as drafted, or send it back for correction?
expected_answer:
This points to artificial splitting, which is not a valid way to move a common requirement into a lower method.
The combined need should control the route, so the case should be tested against LTE logic under Rule 162 rather than the smaller indents.
key_points: Check whether the demand is one requirement in timing, purpose, and funding
Apply the route on aggregate value, not invoice value
Record splitting risk as a high audit concern
Recast the case under the correct method if needed

question: A project coordinator wants to use last year's rate for modular UPS in a fresh Rs. 3,250,000 order because the earlier vendor performed well. The old rate contract has just expired. Can the file rely on the expired terms?
expected_answer:
No. Once the rate contract has expired, it cannot be treated as a fresh procurement basis merely for convenience.
The buyer should start a new process, test GeM first, and then follow the current route for Rs. 3,250,000 under Rule 162.
key_points: Check whether the old contract is still valid
Do not use expired rates as a substitute for fresh competition
Re-test GeM applicability
Restart procurement under Rule 162 if needed

question: The user section says oscilloscope probes must match an existing system and wants to treat the Rs. 1,560,000 purchase as proprietary from a sole authorized dealer. What should be checked before accepting that logic? The price looks attractive, so the team wants to overlook a control weakness. The draft note cites PAC logic even though the facts look closer to standardization than exclusivity.
expected_answer:
Brand continuity alone is not automatically the same as proprietary exclusivity.
The file should separate standardization from true sole-source justification, record why alternatives are impractical, and use PAC or another valid single-source basis only if the facts meet Rule 166.
key_points: Distinguish standardization from pure proprietary claim
Verify whether alternatives can meet compatibility needs
Require technical justification from competent authority
Use single-source logic only when facts actually support it

question: The internal finance officer wants to buy deep freezer compressor worth Rs. 2,610,000 from a local vendor because the same item looks cheaper outside GeM. GeM shows a similar listing. Can the buyer leave GeM on price alone? The technical team treats brand continuity as proprietary, while stores treats it as a competition issue.
expected_answer:
No. Price alone is usually not enough to bypass GeM when the item is available there.
The file should first examine GeM applicability under Rule 149; only a real specification gap, non-availability, or properly recorded exception can justify moving to LTE.
key_points: Check GeM availability first
Treat lower offline price as insufficient by itself
Record any specification mismatch or non-availability evidence
After a valid GeM departure, use the normal value route under Rule 162

question: A technical evaluation member initiated HVAC control panel procurement at Rs. 1,560,000 for a grant closing this quarter, but the urgency exists largely because the old AMC was not renewed in time. Can emergency logic still be used without qualification? Would you clear the note as drafted, or send it back for correction?
expected_answer:
Not cleanly. A preventable planning lapse weakens the case for treating the matter as a pure emergency.
The file may still need expedited handling, but it should acknowledge the planning failure and avoid using urgency as a blanket excuse to ignore normal controls.
key_points: Distinguish genuine emergency from avoidable delay
Do not let urgency automatically displace normal controls
Record the planning lapse and corrective action
Use only the minimum justified departure from the regular method

question: For calibration gases valued at Rs. 640,000, the L1 bidder is cheapest but failed a key technical parameter during evaluation. The committee is considering L2. Is that path supportable? The note assumes that urgency alone cures gaps in competition. GeM shows similar listings, but the scientist says the required configuration is not visible.
expected_answer:
Yes, but only if L1 is rejected for a clearly recorded technical reason and L2 fully meets the specifications.
The file should show a documented non-responsiveness finding, comparison on the surviving bidders, and fresh approval before award.
key_points: Reject L1 only on recorded, defensible technical grounds
Confirm L2 is technically compliant
Document comparative evaluation after rejection
Obtain approval on the recommended bidder

Not fully. Delivery urgency may justify departure, but the file should show how the timing gap was actually assessed.
A conclusion without comparison evidence is weaker than a note that traces the deadline problem concretely.
key_points: Support delivery-urgency claim with facts
Compare available timelines where possible
Do not rely on bare assertion
Link urgency to the procurement need

question: A department wants to use an old offline rate contract for portable gas detector even though equivalent options are visible on GeM. Which source should be examined first?
expected_answer:
GeM should be examined first because current availability there can control sourcing before the old offline arrangement is treated as relevant.
An old convenient channel does not automatically outrank a live mandatory platform path.
key_points: Prioritize current GeM availability check
Do not assume old offline arrangements override platform logic
Record why any non-GeM source remains justified
Then apply route and approval logic

question: For ultra-low freezer, GeM shows broadly similar products but not the exact specification needed. What is the compliant response?
expected_answer:
The buyer should document the specification gap rather than making a bare assertion that GeM is unsuitable.
Once the mismatch is recorded, the case can move to the normal value route for Rs. 4,800,000 under Rule 162.
key_points: Record the exact specification gap
Keep evidence of the GeM search
Do not rely on vague non-feasibility wording
Then apply the normal offline route

question: In practical file work under Rule 155, at what point does the committee route stop being available if quotations for inverter batteries have already started but the value picture shifts for a grant closing this quarter? Two quotations came from sister concerns using nearly identical commercial terms.
expected_answer:
It stops being safe when the controlling estimated value moves beyond the LPC band.
If the realistic procurement value crosses that ceiling, the file should be re-tested under the next route instead of clinging to the earlier committee process.
key_points: LPC availability depends on the controlling value band
Started process does not justify staying in the wrong slab
Revise the estimate if needed
Shift route when the band changes

question: Under Rule 166, what must exist beyond the phrase 'single source' before a proprietary purchase of office workstation becomes supportable?
expected_answer:
The file needs a real basis for exclusivity, usually backed by competent technical certification and reasons why alternatives are not workable.
Without that, 'single source' is just a label rather than a justified departure from competition.
key_points: Single-source label is not enough
Need technical basis for exclusivity
PAC should come from competent authority
Alternative availability must be examined

question: For an approval note relying on Rule 149, what factual showing normally justifies stepping away from GeM in a Rs. 500,001 purchase of ELISA reader rather than merely preferring an offline seller? A stale manual extract in the file still mentions the older Rs. 2.5 lakh threshold.
expected_answer:
The file should show non-availability, material specification mismatch, or another recorded exception, not just convenience or a lower informal quote.
A defensible departure depends on evidence of why GeM could not meet the requirement on the facts.
key_points: Price preference alone is weak
Need evidence of non-availability or mismatch
Record the departure basis explicitly
Only then move to the normal procurement route

question: In practical file work under Rule 162, what is the real control purpose behind inviting multiple firms for laboratory dishwasher rather than treating one known source as enough?
expected_answer:
The point is to preserve a meaningful test of competition and reasonableness within a limited market.
If the file jumps straight to one source without proving why others are unavailable, it loses the protection that limited competition was meant to provide.
key_points: Multiple invitations protect competition
One known source is not the same as only possible source
Reasonableness is easier to defend with comparative response
Explain low-response situations separately

First document the GeM search and the mismatch or non-availability, then move to the normal value-based route.
After the GeM record is complete, the file should proceed through LPC under Rule 155 with the usual approvals and comparative documentation.

Record mismatch or non-availability clearly
Then apply Rule 155 on value

question: A PAC has been drafted for tissue culture flasks, but the actual reason is compatibility with an existing line rather than true market exclusivity. How should that be treated?
expected_answer:
The file should state the compatibility or standardization reason honestly instead of disguising it as pure exclusivity.
Single-source approval may still be possible on facts, but the technical basis should match the real ground being used.
key_points: Describe the true basis for single-source choice
Do not mislabel standardization as pure exclusivity
Require technical reasoning on compatibility
Keep the route aligned with the actual facts

question: If gas chromatograph column exceeds Rs. 5,000,000, what extra caution should the file apply before treating the case as PAC-based? GeM shows similar listings, but the scientist says the required configuration is not visible.

Higher value does not change the meaning of PAC, but it increases the need for precise justification, approval discipline, and scrutiny of alternatives.

Justification should be specific and robust

Alternative-source analysis should be visible

A single valid offer does not automatically make the award unsafe, but it does require recorded scrutiny of competition and reasonableness.
The committee should review publicity, specification restrictiveness, urgency, and value for money before deciding whether to re-tender or proceed with competent approval under Rule 162.
key_points: Test whether competition was adequate
Examine if specifications were too restrictive
Record price reasonableness and urgency if proceeding
Take competent authority approval on the single-offer decision

question: The base price for DNA extraction kit was noted as Rs. 3,610,000, but mandatory freight, installation, and AMC bring the realistic total to Rs. 3,790,000. The draft note still wants to use the lower route chosen on base price. Which valuation should control?
expected_answer:
The controlling value should be the realistic procurement value, not the stripped base price.
If mandatory charges move the case upward, the route should be re-tested on Rs. 3,790,000 and may need to shift to LTE under Rule 162.
key_points: Aggregate mandatory cost components
Do not choose route on an artificially reduced base price
Revise the estimate if the total changes the slab
Re-open the route if the controlling band changes

question: A technical evaluation member initiated ultra-low freezer procurement at Rs. 6,200,000 for a cleanroom restart, but the urgency exists largely because the old AMC was not renewed in time. Can emergency logic still be used without qualification? Two quotations came from sister concerns using nearly identical commercial terms.
expected_answer:
Not cleanly. A preventable planning lapse weakens the case for treating the matter as a pure emergency.
The file may still need expedited handling, but it should acknowledge the planning failure and avoid using urgency as a blanket excuse to ignore normal controls.
key_points: Distinguish genuine emergency from avoidable delay
Do not let urgency automatically displace normal controls
Record the planning lapse and corrective action
Use only the minimum justified departure from the regular method

expected_answer:
The committee should not jump straight to award on an overshoot without re-examining reasonableness and approval.
It should record market assessment, consider re-tendering if prices look abnormal, and obtain revised sanction if the higher value is still justified.

A single valid offer does not automatically make the award unsafe, but it does require recorded scrutiny of competition and reasonableness.
The committee should review publicity, specification restrictiveness, urgency, and value for money before deciding whether to re-tender or proceed with competent approval under Rule 161.
key_points: Test whether competition was adequate
Examine if specifications were too restrictive
Record price reasonableness and urgency if proceeding
Take competent authority approval on the single-offer decision

question: The base price for safety shower valve set was noted as Rs. 1,925,000, but mandatory freight, installation, and AMC bring the realistic total to Rs. 1,965,000. The draft note still wants to use the lower route chosen on base price. Which valuation should control? The price looks attractive, so the team wants to overlook a control weakness.
expected_answer:
The controlling value should be the realistic procurement value, not the stripped base price.
If mandatory charges move the case upward, the route should be re-tested on Rs. 1,965,000 and may need to shift to LTE under Rule 162.
key_points: Aggregate mandatory cost components
Do not choose route on an artificially reduced base price
Revise the estimate if the total changes the slab
Re-open the route if the controlling band changes

question: A indenting scientist initiated cryovials procurement at Rs. 1,560,000 for a monsoon preparedness drive, but the urgency exists largely because the old AMC was not renewed in time. Can emergency logic still be used without qualification? The user section says the item is unique, but gives no technical comparison note.
expected_answer:
Not cleanly. A preventable planning lapse weakens the case for treating the matter as a pure emergency.
The file may still need expedited handling, but it should acknowledge the planning failure and avoid using urgency as a blanket excuse to ignore normal controls.
key_points: Distinguish genuine emergency from avoidable delay
Do not let urgency automatically displace normal controls
Record the planning lapse and corrective action
Use only the minimum justified departure from the regular method

question: A section head wants to use last year's rate for HVAC control panel in a fresh Rs. 1,980,000 order because the earlier vendor performed well. The old rate contract has just expired. Can the file rely on the expired terms? Two quotations came from sister concerns using nearly identical commercial terms.
expected_answer:
No. Once the rate contract has expired, it cannot be treated as a fresh procurement basis merely for convenience.
The buyer should start a new process, test GeM first, and then follow the current route for Rs. 1,980,000 under Rule 162.
key_points: Check whether the old contract is still valid
Do not use expired rates as a substitute for fresh competition
Re-test GeM applicability
Restart procurement under Rule 162 if needed

question: The user section says liquid nitrogen hose must match an existing system and wants to treat the Rs. 915,000 purchase as proprietary from a GeM-listed reseller. What should be checked before accepting that logic? The note assumes that urgency alone cures gaps in competition. The draft note cites PAC logic even though the facts look closer to standardization than exclusivity.
expected_answer:
Brand continuity alone is not automatically the same as proprietary exclusivity.
The file should separate standardization from true sole-source justification, record why alternatives are impractical, and use PAC or another valid single-source basis only if the facts meet Rule 166.
key_points: Distinguish standardization from pure proprietary claim
Verify whether alternatives can meet compatibility needs
Require technical justification from competent authority
Use single-source logic only when facts actually support it

question: For printer cartridges valued at Rs. 499,500, the L1 bidder is cheapest but failed a key technical parameter during evaluation. The committee is considering L2. Is that path supportable? The bid file mixes route-selection logic with approval-power logic as if they were the same test.
expected_answer:
Yes, but only if L1 is rejected for a clearly recorded technical reason and L2 fully meets the specifications.
The file should show a documented non-responsiveness finding, comparison on the surviving bidders, and fresh approval before award.
key_points: Reject L1 only on recorded, defensible technical grounds
Confirm L2 is technically compliant
Document comparative evaluation after rejection
Obtain approval on the recommended bidder

No. Multiple capable supply channels weaken a pure proprietary argument unless another single-source basis is proved.
The file should distinguish product authenticity from source exclusivity before deciding on PAC logic.
key_points: Authenticity is not the same as source exclusivity
Multiple dealers undercut a pure PAC claim
Separate OEM genuineness from procurement route
Use competition if alternatives are available

question: A failed competitive tender is followed by a proposal to buy water purification cartridges from one source. Does the failed tender automatically eliminate the need for PAC reasoning?
expected_answer:
No. Failed competition may support a single-source decision in some cases, but it does not magically convert the case into a proprietary purchase.
The file should explain the market outcome, why re-tendering is not useful, and what legal basis now supports the one-source route.
key_points: Failed tender is not automatic PAC
Record why competition failed
Explain why re-tendering is not preferable
State the actual single-source basis now being used

question: For oxygen sensors worth Rs. 310,000, when does a PAC mean a Proprietary Article Certificate rather than just a convenient single-source note?
expected_answer:
It means a Proprietary Article Certificate only when the file is using genuine proprietary or otherwise justified single-source logic under the PAC framework.
A convenience-based vendor preference is weaker and should not be labelled as PAC procurement unless exclusivity is actually demonstrated.
key_points: PAC here means Proprietary Article Certificate
PAC is tied to justified single-source procurement
Convenience is not enough
Exclusivity must be shown on file

question: The PAC for safety shower valve set is signed by an administrative officer because the scientist is on leave. Is the certificate still safe to rely on?
expected_answer:

The normal route and the Make in India test should be read together, but the threshold route is usually identified first and then the bidder-eligibility or preference issue is applied within that tender context.
What matters is that local-supplier preference is not treated as a substitute for choosing the base procurement method.
key_points: Do not let Make in India replace route selection
Identify base procurement method first
Apply eligibility or preference within the chosen tender context
Record both layers of reasoning

question: What makes the aggregate value matter more than individual line items when several small conductivity meter-related purchases serve one project objective for a student training programme starting next week?
expected_answer:
Because procurement control targets the real requirement, not the arithmetic of how it is split on paper.
If common timing, funding, and purpose show one requirement, the aggregate better reflects the competition route and audit risk.
key_points: Aggregate value tests the real requirement
Line-item treatment can hide route circumvention
Purpose, timing, and funding help decide clubbing
Audit looks at substance over invoice structure

question: From an audit perspective, why does separation of duties matter in a Rs. 49,900 procurement file for office workstation even when everyone involved appears honest and technically competent?
expected_answer:
Because procurement controls are designed to survive personnel changes, pressure, and hindsight, not just to reflect present trust.

Honesty does not remove structural risk
Independent scrutiny improves defensibility

question: How does checking GeM logically come before debating whether LC-MS solvent bottles at about Rs. 2,610,000 falls in direct purchase, LPC, LTE, or OTE? The user section says the item is unique, but gives no technical comparison note.
expected_answer:
Because the route-by-value question only becomes meaningful after the sourcing constraint is checked.
If the item is available on GeM, Rule 149 can control the sourcing path first; only then does the threshold route determine the compliant offline or downstream method.

Value slabs apply after GeM logic is tested
Do not treat route and source platform as separate worlds
Record why GeM does or does not control

First document the GeM search and the mismatch or non-availability, then move to the normal value-based route.
After the GeM record is complete, the file should proceed through LTE under Rule 162 with the usual approvals and comparative documentation.
key_points: Document GeM search results first
Record mismatch or non-availability clearly
Then apply Rule 162 on value
Keep approval and comparison records in sequence

question: A March-approved purchase of ICP-MS torch assembly will spill into the next financial year. What sequence of checks should the dealing hand complete before issue of supply order or booking of expenditure? What is the correct workflow from this point?
expected_answer:
The officer should check budget provision, approval validity, and booking year before assuming continuity.
If any of those controls fail, the file needs renewal, regularization, or revised sanction before moving further.
key_points: Check budget availability in the relevant year
Review validity of prior approval
Confirm how expenditure will be booked
Regularize or renew sanction if needed

question: Quotations for LC-MS solvent bottles were sought on an estimate below a threshold, but the realistic total is now higher because mandatory charges were omitted. What is the correct workflow from this point?
expected_answer:
The estimate should be corrected first, then the route should be re-tested on the revised total.
If the revised value changes the governing slab, the buyer should not continue the old process as though the valuation mistake never happened.
key_points: Revise the estimate before continuing
Re-test the route on total value
Change method if the slab changes
Record why the original estimate was incomplete

question: The GeM portal remained inaccessible while calibration gases was needed urgently. How should the file move, step by step, if an offline purchase is contemplated?
expected_answer:
Capture downtime evidence first, then record urgency, then choose the offline route that matches the value band.
The file should also explain why waiting for portal restoration would have harmed the requirement.
key_points: Collect downtime proof
Record urgency and impact of delay
Apply the correct offline value route
Preserve approval and supporting justification

question: Several departments want related weatherproof field laptop purchases from the same budget head within the same quarter. What sequence should be followed to decide whether the demands must be clubbed?
expected_answer:
First test purpose, timing, funding, and interchangeability of the demands; then estimate the aggregate if they are really one requirement.
Only after that should the buyer choose the route and document why clubbing was or was not required.
key_points: Test whether the demands are truly related
Use aggregate value if they form one requirement
Choose route after clubbing analysis
Record reasons for clubbing or separation

question: A repeat order to the same vendor for incubator controller is being considered. What checks should be completed in sequence before the proposal is cleared? What is the correct workflow from this point?
expected_answer:

Only after those tests should the approval note treat repeat ordering as a serious option.

Take approval on the repeat-order rationale

First test purpose, timing, funding, and interchangeability of the demands; then estimate the aggregate if they are really one requirement.
Only after that should the buyer choose the route and document why clubbing was or was not required.
key_points: Test whether the demands are truly related
Use aggregate value if they form one requirement
Choose route after clubbing analysis
Record reasons for clubbing or separation

question: The evaluation committee wants to reject L1 for weatherproof field laptop and consider L2. What file sequence keeps that decision defensible? The technical team treats brand continuity as proprietary, while stores treats it as a competition issue.
expected_answer:
The file should record the technical or responsiveness failure first, then compare the surviving compliant bidders, then place a reasoned recommendation for approval.
Skipping directly from L1 rejection to award recommendation is weaker than showing the full evaluation chain.
key_points: Record L1 rejection grounds first
Evaluate remaining compliant bidders afresh
Maintain comparative reasoning on file
Seek approval on the final recommendation

question: During bid evaluation for pH meter electrode, a bidder claims local supplier preference. What sequence should the committee follow before applying that benefit?
expected_answer:
The committee should first verify the bidder's declared class and local-content basis, then test value-band eligibility, and only then apply ranking or split-order preference.
Preference should follow verified status, not precede it.
key_points: Check local-content declaration first
Confirm class and eligibility for the value band
Apply preference only after verification
Record the evaluation basis clearly

Not cleanly. A preventable planning lapse weakens the case for treating the matter as a pure emergency.
The file may still need expedited handling, but it should acknowledge the planning failure and avoid using urgency as a blanket excuse to ignore normal controls.
key_points: Distinguish genuine emergency from avoidable delay
Do not let urgency automatically displace normal controls
Record the planning lapse and corrective action
Use only the minimum justified departure from the regular method

question: The project coordinator wants to buy biometric attendance device worth Rs. 3,250,000 from a local vendor because the same item looks cheaper outside GeM. GeM shows a similar listing. Can the buyer leave GeM on price alone? The proposal relies on last year's practice rather than the current routing logic. Should the case move forward, be re-tendered, or be re-framed first?
expected_answer:
No. Price alone is usually not enough to bypass GeM when the item is available there.
The file should first examine GeM applicability under Rule 149; only a real specification gap, non-availability, or properly recorded exception can justify moving to LTE.
key_points: Check GeM availability first
Treat lower offline price as insufficient by itself
Record any specification mismatch or non-availability evidence
After a valid GeM departure, use the normal value route under Rule 162

expected_answer:
No. Once the rate contract has expired, it cannot be treated as a fresh procurement basis merely for convenience.
The buyer should start a new process, test GeM first, and then follow the current route for Rs. 3,750,000 under Rule 162.
key_points: Check whether the old contract is still valid
Do not use expired rates as a substitute for fresh competition
Re-test GeM applicability
Restart procurement under Rule 162 if needed

question: The base price for LC-MS solvent bottles was noted as Rs. 4,745,000, but mandatory freight, installation, and AMC bring the realistic total to Rs. 4,815,000. expected_answer:
The controlling value should be the realistic procurement value, not the stripped base price.
If mandatory charges move the case upward, the route should be re-tested on Rs. 4,815,000 and may need to shift to LTE under Rule 162.
key_points: Aggregate mandatory cost components
Do not choose route on an artificially reduced base price
Revise the estimate if the total changes the slab
Re-open the route if the controlling band changes

expected_answer:
Brand continuity alone is not automatically the same as proprietary exclusivity.

Verify whether alternatives can meet compatibility needs

The file should state the compatibility or standardization reason honestly instead of disguising it as pure exclusivity.
Single-source approval may still be possible on facts, but the technical basis should match the real ground being used.
key_points: Describe the true basis for single-source choice
Do not mislabel standardization as pure exclusivity
Require technical reasoning on compatibility
Keep the route aligned with the actual facts

question: A vendor says only it can supply ultra-low freezer, but no competent technical officer has issued a PAC. Can the buyer safely proceed as proprietary?
expected_answer:

Need competent technical certification
Check alternative sources
Do not jump to proprietary route on supplier assertion alone

question: The PAC for glass reaction vessel is signed by an administrative officer because the scientist is on leave. Is the certificate still safe to rely on?
expected_answer:
Usually no. The problem is not just signature formality; it is the lack of competent technical certification.

PAC needs technical competence
Authority defect affects audit defensibility
Re-issue through proper signatory

question: A failed competitive tender is followed by a proposal to buy laboratory dishwasher from one source. Does the failed tender automatically eliminate the need for PAC reasoning? The user wing cites speed, while finance cites the normal competition route.
expected_answer:
No. Failed competition may support a single-source decision in some cases, but it does not magically convert the case into a proprietary purchase.
The file should explain the market outcome, why re-tendering is not useful, and what legal basis now supports the one-source route.
key_points: Failed tender is not automatic PAC
Record why competition failed
Explain why re-tendering is not preferable
State the actual single-source basis now being used

question: For thermal cycler at Rs. 915,000, what additional record should accompany a PAC if the buyer wants the single-source route to look credible in audit? Which route should control?
expected_answer:
The PAC should be supported by a clear note on why competition is not feasible and, where possible, by market or compatibility evidence.
The certificate is central, but the file should also show the factual trail behind it.
key_points: Attach reasoned justification behind the PAC
Show why competition is infeasible
Preserve technical or market evidence
Keep approval trail with the PAC

At minimum, the file should show downtime evidence, attempted access, timing, and why waiting was not practical.
Without that, the offline move can look like convenience rather than necessity.
key_points: Capture downtime proof
Record timestamps and attempts
Explain urgency or impracticality of delay
Link the exception to the actual procurement need

question: A department wants to use an old offline rate contract for stainless steel worktable even though equivalent options are visible on GeM. Which source should be examined first?
expected_answer:
GeM should be examined first because current availability there can control sourcing before the old offline arrangement is treated as relevant.
An old convenient channel does not automatically outrank a live mandatory platform path.
key_points: Prioritize current GeM availability check
Do not assume old offline arrangements override platform logic
Record why any non-GeM source remains justified
Then apply route and approval logic

question: An officer says GeM was checked for sample storage racks, but the screenshots are missing from the file. How much audit comfort should that statement provide?

The committee should not jump straight to award on an overshoot without re-examining reasonableness and approval.
It should record market assessment, consider re-tendering if prices look abnormal, and obtain revised sanction if the higher value is still justified.
key_points: Compare the quoted rate with current market conditions
Consider whether re-tendering is warranted
Seek revised estimate or sanction if proceeding
Record competent approval on the revised financial position

question: The GeM portal is down while sample storage racks worth Rs. 1,180,000 is urgently needed for a cleanroom restart. The section wants to buy offline immediately. Record urgency and why delay was unacceptable

question: The base price for printer cartridges was noted as Rs. 1,925,000, but mandatory freight, installation, and AMC bring the realistic total to Rs. 2,105,000. The controlling value should be the realistic procurement value, not the stripped base price.

Do not choose route on an artificially reduced base price

question: The technical evaluation member wants to buy sample storage racks worth Rs. 5,000,001 from a local vendor because the same item looks cheaper outside GeM. GeM shows a similar listing. Can the buyer leave GeM on price alone? The proposal relies on last year's practice rather than the current routing logic.
expected_answer:
No. Price alone is usually not enough to bypass GeM when the item is available there.
The file should first examine GeM applicability under Rule 149; only a real specification gap, non-availability, or properly recorded exception can justify moving to OTE.
key_points: Check GeM availability first
Treat lower offline price as insufficient by itself
Record any specification mismatch or non-availability evidence
After a valid GeM departure, use the normal value route under Rule 161

question: An RFID access controller case estimated at Rs. 1,180,000 was opened through LTE, but only one valid bid was received. The user division wants immediate placement because the work is time-bound. What is the defensible next step? What is the safest defensible decision on file?
expected_answer:
A single valid offer does not automatically make the award unsafe, but it does require recorded scrutiny of competition and reasonableness.
The committee should review publicity, specification restrictiveness, urgency, and value for money before deciding whether to re-tender or proceed with competent approval under Rule 162.

Examine if specifications were too restrictive

Yes, but only if L1 is rejected for a clearly recorded technical reason and L2 fully meets the specifications.
The file should show a documented non-responsiveness finding, comparison on the surviving bidders, and fresh approval before award.
key_points: Reject L1 only on recorded, defensible technical grounds
Confirm L2 is technically compliant
Document comparative evaluation after rejection
Obtain approval on the recommended bidder

question: All compliant bids for laser particle counter are above the estimate; the best offer is Rs. 5,345,000 against a sanctioned estimate of Rs. 5,250,000. What should the committee do before award? The draft note cites PAC logic even though the facts look closer to standardization than exclusivity.
expected_answer:
The committee should not jump straight to award on an overshoot without re-examining reasonableness and approval.
It should record market assessment, consider re-tendering if prices look abnormal, and obtain revised sanction if the higher value is still justified.
key_points: Compare the quoted rate with current market conditions
Consider whether re-tendering is warranted
Seek revised estimate or sanction if proceeding
Record competent approval on the revised financial position

question: The purchase committee convener wants to buy modular UPS worth Rs. 1,180,000 from a local vendor because the same item looks cheaper outside GeM. GeM shows a similar listing. Can the buyer leave GeM on price alone?
expected_answer:
No. Price alone is usually not enough to bypass GeM when the item is available there.
The file should first examine GeM applicability under Rule 149; only a real specification gap, non-availability, or properly recorded exception can justify moving to LTE.
key_points: Check GeM availability first
Treat lower offline price as insufficient by itself
Record any specification mismatch or non-availability evidence
After a valid GeM departure, use the normal value route under Rule 162

question: The GeM portal is down while incubator controller worth Rs. 1,980,000 is urgently needed for a cleanroom restart. The section wants to buy offline immediately. What documentation makes that choice defensible? GeM shows similar listings, but the scientist says the required configuration is not visible. Would you clear the note as drafted, or send it back for correction?
expected_answer:
The case needs evidence, not just a statement that the portal was unavailable.
Screenshots, timestamps, urgency justification, and a note on why waiting was impractical should appear on file before any alternative route is taken.
key_points: Capture GeM downtime evidence
Record urgency and why delay was unacceptable
Explain why the alternative route was necessary
Apply the normal value route once the GeM exception is justified

expected_answer:
The controlling value should be the realistic procurement value, not the stripped base price.
If mandatory charges move the case upward, the route should be re-tested on Rs. 95,000 and may need to shift to LPC under Rule 155.
key_points: Aggregate mandatory cost components
Do not choose route on an artificially reduced base price
Revise the estimate if the total changes the slab
Re-open the route if the controlling band changes

question: The indenting scientist wants to buy LC-MS solvent bottles worth Rs. 310,000 from a local vendor because the same item looks cheaper outside GeM. GeM shows a similar listing. Can the buyer leave GeM on price alone? GeM shows similar listings, but the scientist says the required configuration is not visible.
expected_answer:
No. Price alone is usually not enough to bypass GeM when the item is available there.
The file should first examine GeM applicability under Rule 149; only a real specification gap, non-availability, or properly recorded exception can justify moving to LPC.
key_points: Check GeM availability first
Treat lower offline price as insufficient by itself
Record any specification mismatch or non-availability evidence
After a valid GeM departure, use the normal value route under Rule 155

question: The GeM portal is down while ICP-MS torch assembly worth Rs. 1,560,000 is urgently needed for a grant closing this quarter. The section wants to buy offline immediately. What documentation makes that choice defensible? The price looks attractive, so the team wants to overlook a control weakness. The draft note cites PAC logic even though the facts look closer to standardization than exclusivity.
expected_answer:
The case needs evidence, not just a statement that the portal was unavailable.
Screenshots, timestamps, urgency justification, and a note on why waiting was impractical should appear on file before any alternative route is taken.
key_points: Capture GeM downtime evidence
Record urgency and why delay was unacceptable
Explain why the alternative route was necessary
Apply the normal value route once the GeM exception is justified

question: All compliant bids for mass spectrometer software license are above the estimate; the best offer is Rs. 375,000 against a sanctioned estimate of Rs. 125,000. What should the committee do before award? Which route should control?
expected_answer:

It should record market assessment, consider re-tendering if prices look abnormal, and obtain revised sanction if the higher value is still justified.
key_points: Compare the quoted rate with current market conditions
Consider whether re-tendering is warranted

Because undocumented reasoning cannot be reconstructed safely after the dispute begins.
A sound decision that is weakly recorded may fail audit or complaint review because the institution cannot show how it reached the conclusion.
key_points: Documentation preserves the reasoning trail
Post-award defence depends on the file, not memory
Sparse notes increase complaint vulnerability
Correct decisions still need recorded support

question: Why does treating standardization and proprietary purchase as interchangeable lead to weak reasoning for server rack for a safety-critical replacement?
expected_answer:
Because the two ideas answer different questions: compatibility versus exclusivity.
If the file does not separate them, it may skip competition where alternatives could still meet the technical need.
key_points: Standardization is not automatically exclusivity
Compatibility should be proved, not assumed
Mislabeling can overstate single-source justification
Competition may still be possible

question: Why are outdated threshold references dangerous even when the final route chosen for a Rs. 50,001 ELISA reader case happens to look reasonable on the facts? The note assumes that urgency alone cures gaps in competition.

Because procurement control targets the real requirement, not the arithmetic of how it is split on paper.

Convenience is weaker than proprietary necessity

It means a Proprietary Article Certificate only when the file is using genuine proprietary or otherwise justified single-source logic under the PAC framework.
A convenience-based vendor preference is weaker and should not be labelled as PAC procurement unless exclusivity is actually demonstrated.
key_points: PAC here means Proprietary Article Certificate
PAC is tied to justified single-source procurement
Convenience is not enough
Exclusivity must be shown on file

question: A buyer says a PAC is unnecessary because everyone in the lab already knows that spectrophotometer lamp normally comes only from the OEM. Is that enough?
expected_answer:
No. Shared internal belief is weaker than a documented Proprietary Article Certificate backed by technical reasons.
The file should rely on recorded evidence rather than institutional memory or habit.
key_points: Institutional habit is not PAC evidence
Need documented proprietary reasoning
Technical authority should certify the claim
File record matters more than oral understanding

question: Who should issue the PAC for biometric attendance device if the lab wants a single-source purchase to stand up in audit? Which route should control?
expected_answer:
The PAC should come from a competent serving technical authority who can explain why the item is proprietary or otherwise requires that source.
It should not be issued only by the procurement desk or by someone without current technical authority over the requirement.
key_points: Require competent serving technical authority
Technical reasoning should support the PAC
Administrative staff alone should not issue it
Authority and expertise both matter

question: For ultra-low freezer at Rs. 915,000, what additional record should accompany a PAC if the buyer wants the single-source route to look credible in audit?
expected_answer:
The PAC should be supported by a clear note on why competition is not feasible and, where possible, by market or compatibility evidence.
The certificate is central, but the file should also show the factual trail behind it.
key_points: Attach reasoned justification behind the PAC
Show why competition is infeasible
Preserve technical or market evidence
Keep approval trail with the PAC

question: The PAC for qPCR plates is signed by an administrative officer because the scientist is on leave. Is the certificate still safe to rely on? The bid file mixes route-selection logic with approval-power logic as if they were the same test. Would you clear the note as drafted, or send it back for correction?
expected_answer:
Usually no. The problem is not just signature formality; it is the lack of competent technical certification.
The file should wait for or obtain a technically competent PAC signatory if proprietary logic is to be defended.
key_points: Administrative signature is not enough
PAC needs technical competence
Authority defect affects audit defensibility
Re-issue through proper signatory

The file should check whether the original order was competitive, whether the price is unchanged or lower, and whether the validity conditions still support repetition.
Only after those tests should the approval note treat repeat ordering as a serious option.
key_points: Verify competitive origin of the earlier order
Check price continuity or reduction
Review validity period and continuing need
Take approval on the repeat-order rationale

question: Quotations for microscope camera were sought on an estimate below a threshold, but the realistic total is now higher because mandatory charges were omitted. What is the correct workflow from this point?
expected_answer:
The estimate should be corrected first, then the route should be re-tested on the revised total.
If the revised value changes the governing slab, the buyer should not continue the old process as though the valuation mistake never happened.
key_points: Revise the estimate before continuing
Re-test the route on total value
Change method if the slab changes
Record why the original estimate was incomplete

question: Several departments want related deep freezer compressor purchases from the same budget head within the same quarter. What sequence should be followed to decide whether the demands must be clubbed?

First test purpose, timing, funding, and interchangeability of the demands; then estimate the aggregate if they are really one requirement.
Only after that should the buyer choose the route and document why clubbing was or was not required.
key_points: Test whether the demands are truly related
Use aggregate value if they form one requirement
Choose route after clubbing analysis
Record reasons for clubbing or separation

A PAC is meant to establish justified exclusivity through competent technical certification, not mere commercial convenience.
That distinction matters because single-source procurement should rest on a defensible technical basis, not on habit, loyalty, or ease of purchase.
key_points: PAC is about defensible exclusivity
Convenience is weaker than proprietary necessity
Technical authority matters
Single-source risk rises if the file blurs this distinction

question: What makes checking GeM logically come before debating whether portable gas detector at about Rs. 5,000,001 falls in direct purchase, LPC, LTE, or OTE? The proposal relies on last year's practice rather than the current routing logic.
expected_answer:
Because the route-by-value question only becomes meaningful after the sourcing constraint is checked.
If the item is available on GeM, Rule 149 can control the sourcing path first; only then does the threshold route determine the compliant offline or downstream method.
key_points: GeM is a sourcing gate, not just another route detail
Value slabs apply after GeM logic is tested
Do not treat route and source platform as separate worlds
Record why GeM does or does not control

question: How does verifying local-content claims before using purchase preference matter more in a higher-value tender for nitrogen generator service kit than in casual low-value buying? What is the safest defensible decision on file?
expected_answer:
Because preference affects eligibility, ranking, and award outcome more seriously as procurement value and competition intensity increase.
If local-content status is wrong, the tender may be distorted at the evaluation stage rather than merely at a minor filing stage.
key_points: Local-content status can change eligibility and preference
Higher-value tenders magnify evaluation consequences
Verification should precede award benefit
Misclassification can taint the final ranking

question: How does treating standardization and proprietary purchase as interchangeable lead to weak reasoning for gas chromatograph column for a plant maintenance outage? The user wing cites speed, while finance cites the normal competition route.
expected_answer:
Because the two ideas answer different questions: compatibility versus exclusivity.
If the file does not separate them, it may skip competition where alternatives could still meet the technical need.
key_points: Standardization is not automatically exclusivity
Compatibility should be proved, not assumed
Mislabeling can overstate single-source justification
Competition may still be possible

question: Why are outdated threshold references dangerous even when the final route chosen for a Rs. 820,000 calibration gases case happens to look reasonable on the facts? The note assumes that urgency alone cures gaps in competition.
expected_answer:
Because a file that relies on stale thresholds is vulnerable even if the outcome accidentally lands near the right route.
The concern is not only the result but whether the decision was made through the current controlling framework.
key_points: Correct result reached through wrong logic is still risky
Current threshold table should be cited explicitly
Outdated references weaken defensibility
Audit checks reasoning chain, not outcome alone

question: From an audit perspective, why does separation of duties matter in a Rs. 47,800 procurement file for XRD sample holder even when everyone involved appears honest and technically competent? A stale manual extract in the file still mentions the older Rs. 2.5 lakh threshold.
expected_answer:
Because procurement controls are designed to survive personnel changes, pressure, and hindsight, not just to reflect present trust.
Independent scrutiny reduces the chance that one person's preference silently becomes the institution's untested decision.
key_points: Separation protects institutional integrity
Honesty does not remove structural risk
Independent scrutiny improves defensibility
Audit tests process robustness, not only intent

question: Why should urgency caused by internal delay carry less weight than urgency caused by an external breakdown or safety risk in a DNA extraction kit procurement? The file note treats separate invoices as proof that the demand is separate.
expected_answer:
Because self-created urgency is weaker as a justification for relaxing competition or documentation.
The file still has to solve the present need, but audit will ask whether the departure was unavoidable or created by poor planning.
key_points: Separate genuine urgency from avoidable delay
Internal planning failure weakens exception logic
Expediency does not erase control obligations
Corrective planning should be recorded

question: What makes the aggregate value matter more than individual line items when several small weatherproof field laptop-related purchases serve one project objective for a student training programme starting next week?
expected_answer:
Because procurement control targets the real requirement, not the arithmetic of how it is split on paper.
If common timing, funding, and purpose show one requirement, the aggregate better reflects the competition route and audit risk.
key_points: Aggregate value tests the real requirement
Line-item treatment can hide route circumvention
Purpose, timing, and funding help decide clubbing
Audit looks at substance over invoice structure

question: Why does sparse file documentation make post-award complaints on precision weighing pans harder to defend even if the committee's judgment was probably correct?
expected_answer:
Because undocumented reasoning cannot be reconstructed safely after the dispute begins.
A sound decision that is weakly recorded may fail audit or complaint review because the institution cannot show how it reached the conclusion.
key_points: Documentation preserves the reasoning trail
Post-award defence depends on the file, not memory
Sparse notes increase complaint vulnerability
Correct decisions still need recorded support
